q1: SELECT f1.drinker, f2.drinker FROM (SELECT drinker, SUM(times_a_week) AS st FROM frequents GROUP BY drinker) AS f1, (SELECT drinker, SUM(times_a_week) AS st FROM frequents GROUP BY drinker) AS f2 WHERE f1.drinker < f2.drinker AND f1.st = f2.st
q2: SELECT f1.drinker AS drinkerA, f2.drinker AS drinkerB FROM frequents AS f1, frequents AS f2 WHERE f1.drinker < f2.drinker AND f1.drinker <> f2.drinker AND (SELECT SUM(f3.times_a_week) FROM frequents AS f3 WHERE f3.drinker = f1.drinker) = (SELECT SUM(f4.times_a_week) FROM frequents AS f4 WHERE f4.drinker = f2.drinker)

Q2 uses correlated subqueries to compute sums for each row, leading to duplicate (drinkerA, drinkerB) pairs if the same drinker has multiple entries in 'frequents'.
